Based on the quoted language, Clara’s occupancy does **not automatically offset** your $3,400 tax debit. Renting elsewhere is not itself a basis for reimbursement. A cotenant occupancy charge may depend on the governing agreement, local law, whether you were excluded from Unit A, any agreement to pay rent, Unit A’s fair rental value, ownership percentages, and expenses Clara paid.

### Closing reconciliation supported by the current information

| Item | Debit to you | Credit to you |
|---|---:|---:|
| Tax allocation under §4.2: 50/50 regardless of occupancy | $3,400 | — |
| Occupancy offset established by agreement or supporting legal/accounting basis | — | $0 |
| **Net amount currently supported** | **$3,400** | — |

A proposed occupancy adjustment should be listed separately as **unresolved**, not entered as a $3,400 credit merely to reach zero.

### Message to the closing agent or estate representative

> Please show my $3,400 tax allocation under §4.2 separately from any cotenancy occupancy adjustment. Before the reconciliation is finalized, please confirm whether the governing agreement or applicable law permits an occupancy charge concerning Clara’s sole use of Unit A, and provide the calculation, including the relevant period, ownership shares, fair rental value, and expense credits. I do not agree that the absence of an occupancy adjustment has been resolved by the current schedule.

Preserve the issue before signing the final reconciliation. My recommendation is **not** to submit a schedule showing a zero balance unless the offset is supported by the full agreement, applicable law, or written agreement among the parties.
